question_text: Define the terms layer and broiler.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Layer
steps.why: A bird kept for eggs is fed and housed to lay for as long as possible.
common_mistakes: Saying layers are raised for meat.
lines: Layers are birds which are exclusively
raised for the production of eggs.

steps.label: Broiler
steps.why: A bird kept for meat is grown fast and sold young, so it never reaches laying age.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the 8 to 10 week figure.
steps.memory_tip: Broilers are raised for meat and sold at 8 to 10 weeks.
steps.margin_note: Give the age. It is an easy extra point.
lines: Broilers are birds which are raised only for

lines.text: They are raised up to 8 or 10 weeks, then sold

insider_note: This question is asked more often than any other two-mark question in this chapter. One word each decides the mark: eggs for layers, meat for broilers.
